newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says four missile engines discovered.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says four missile engines discovered.

text.p: Iraq said on Monday it had unearthed four destroyed engines from banned ballistic missiles during excavations supervised by U.N. officials.

"The investigations which were carried out jointly by the Iraqi competent authorities and UNSCOM have resulted in discovering four destroyed missile engines in the sites where those missile engines were destroyed a few years ago," said a Foreign Ministry spokesman.
Iraq said it proved its claim to have destroyed all its weapons banned by the United Nations at the end of the 1991 Gulf war.

There was no immediate comment from the officials of UNSCOM, the U.N. Special Commission overseeing destruction of Iraq's weapons of mass destruction, who had expressed suspicion that previous unearthed engines were local products substituted for still-missing imported engines.

Iraqi bulldozers began digging at the site last Tuesday to recover what Iraq said were banned missile components destroyed and buried after Baghdad's troops were driven from Kuwait. Ten U.N. missile experts are supervising the digging.

"The discovery confirms the credibility of what Iraq has always declared, that the destruction process of the missiles was comprehensive and that the allegations on hiding a number of missiles are baseless and merely intelligence games," the spokesman said in a statement distributed by the official Iraqi News Agency INA.
